body.p: The rejection of claims 1, 3 to 6 and 9 to 17 as anticipated by Becker (US
2016/0018793) is overcome by amendment of independent claims 1 and 13 and is traversed.
Independent claims 1 and 13 are directed to a system and a method that use first and
second control units to actuate an aircraft component during different periods. The first control unit controls the actuation of the aircraft component using the first electrical resource device.
Authority to control the aircraft component is with the first control unit during a first period and transfers to a second control unit during a second period.

In addition to transferring authority between the first and second periods, a switching mechanism (claim 1) or switching control (claim 13) transfers authority between the control units in response to a status input from a first electrical resource device. The switching between control units in response to the status input is independent of the switching between the first and second periods.

The independent claims are amended to clarify that the switching due to a status input of the first electrical resource device is separate from the switching between the first and second periods. Support for the amendment is at paragraphs [0046] and [0071] of published Application US 2023/0234699 (App.).

In the embodiment described in the application, control assembly 110 switches authority between the first and second control units by telling the control units which unit is "responsible" and which is "not responsible" for controlling the aircraft component. During normal operations, the control assembly switches authority back and forth between control units such that the first control unit has authority during a first period and the second control unit has authority during a second period. The switching may be "periodically" as the first and second periods repeat. App. para. [0066].

The switching mechanism recited in claim 1 has a "device status input" that indicates the status of the first electrical resource device. Similarly, independent claim 13 recites switching control between the first and second control units based on the status of the first electrical resource device. The device status input and status of the first electrical resource device causes a switch between the first and second control devices that is independent of whether the first or second periods have expired.

The aircraft engines are electrical resource devices in the embodiment described in the application. App. para. [0065]. If a fault occurs in an aircraft engine, a "fault" status is issued. App. para. [0070]. The fault status causes switching mechanism 120 to quickly switch authority away from the control unit associated with the engine with the fault to the control unit associated with the engine not associated with the fault. App. para. [0071].

The independent claims are not anticipated because Becker does not teach a first period during which a first control unit has authority to control an aircraft component and a second period during which a second control unit has authority.

Becker describes data concentrators that control a ventilation system in an aircraft. Becker para. [0012]. A central processing unit selects which of the data concentrators will control the aircraft component. Becker para. [0013]. The selection is based on which data concentrator has the "most robust power supply." Becker para. [0014]. The selection based on the most robust power supply is performed repeatedly, such as every 50 ms to 150 ms. Becker para. [0013].

Becker does not describe switching data concentrators based on a first period or a second period. Becker teaches switching data concentrators based only a characteristic of power supplies, such as which power supply is most robust or which a power supply failed. Becker, paras. [0014] and [0044]. Switching based on a failure or other characteristic of a power supply does not teach the claimed feature of switching based on periods.
The rejection asserts that paragraph [0044] of Becker teaches the claimed feature of
switching based on periods. However, paragraph [0044] does not mention periods or suggest that each of the data concentrators control the ventilator during different periods.

In summary, there is no anticipation because Becker does not disclose the claimed feature of a first control unit that controls actuation of an aircraft component during a first time period and a second control unit that controls actuation during a second time period, in addition to switching between the first and second control units based on a status of an electrical resource device.

Dependent claim 9 requires the first and second periods to repeat. As discussed above, Becker does not disclose switching between first and second periods and would not suggest repeatedly switching between first and second periods.
The rejection of dependent claim 2 as obvious over Becker in view of Uki
(JP 2006142869) is traversed in view of the differences between Becker and claim 1 on which claim 2 depends.

Claim 2 and new claim 18 state that the first control unit actuates a landing gear system, a braking system or a steering system. The rejection applies Uki as teaching actuators for a landing gear and asserts that it would have been obvious to apply the control of actuators in Becker for a ventilation system to controlling a landing gear system based on Uki.

Uki does not suggest controlling actuators such that each actuator has authority to control an aircraft component at different periods. Rather, Uki teaches a primary actuator and a backup actuator. The backup actuator used "in the event of an actuator failure." Uki, para. [0002](English translation).

Uki and Becker do not teach switching between actuators based on periods as recited in the claims. The combination of Uki and Becker would not have rendered obvious the claimed switching between first and second control units based on periods.
The rejection of dependent claims 7 and 8 as obvious over Becker is traversed in view of the differences between Becker and claim 1 on which claims 7 and 8 depend.

Claims 7 and 8 require the switching mechanism to be part of the first or second control units. Claims 7 and 8 depend on claim 1 which, as stated above, requires switching between first and second control units based on periods and separately based on a status indicator of an electrical resource device. Becker does not teach switching between data concentrators based on periods and would not have rendered obvious the claimed invention that requires switching based on periods.
New Claims

Claim 18 depends on method claim 13 and requires the electrical resource device to be an aircraft engine and the aircraft component to be at least one of a landing gear bay door, landing gear extension and retraction mechanism, a wheel braking system or a wheel steering system. Support for claim 18 is in paragraphs [008], [0018] and [0063] to [0065] of the Application. Becker does not show using an aircraft engine to provide an electrical resource or a control unit that actuates a landing gear bay door, landing gear extension and retraction mechanism, wheel braking system or a wheel steering system.

Independent claim 19 is directed to a landing gear control system with first and second control units that apply electrical power generated by first and second aircraft engines to a landing gear component. Authority for controlling the landing gear component switches between the first and second control units based on both first and second periods and based on a status of at least one of the aircraft engines.
Becker does not disclose control units that actuate a landing gear based on power
generated by aircraft engines. Becker also does not teach switching between control units based on both first and second periods, and based on a status of an aircraft engine.
Claim Interpretation Under 35 USC 112(f) Does Not Apply

The term "switch mechanism" is a structural term and should not be interpreted under 35 USC 112(f). The term "switch" has a dictionary definition of "a device for making, breaking, or changing the connections in an electrical circuit." Merriam-Webster (online). A person of ordinary skill in the art would understand that a switch is a structure. Because it recites the structure of a switch, the term switch mechanism should not be treated under section 112(f).
